label: May 1918
headline: Breakthrough on the Aisne
deck: A surprise offensive on the Chemin des Dames reaches the Marne
caption: French refugees with carts crowd a road south from Soissons
body: Early on 27 May some four thousand German guns open fire on the Chemin des Dames ridge, held by French divisions and by British divisions sent there to rest after the battles of the spring. Within hours the ridge is lost, and German troops cross the Aisne on bridges the defenders had no time to destroy.
Soissons falls on 29 May. On 30 May the Germans stand on the Marne at Château-Thierry, some fifty miles from Paris, and the city hears the guns again.
At Cantigny, on 28 May, the American 1st Division makes its first attack of the war, takes the village and holds it against counter-attacks.
In Siberia the Czechoslovak Legion, travelling east along the railway towards Vladivostok, rises against the Bolshevik authorities.
briefs: Romania signs the Treaty of Bucharest
The old cruiser Vindictive is sunk to block Ostend
Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan declare their independence
